text: Peace be upon you and God's mercy and blessings. Today I want to begin with two pieces of news. The first is that Egypt is now officially going to produce whole-grain bread and other whole-grain products.
The second is that the United States and some European countries destroyed millions of eggs that were contaminated with Salmonella bacteria, and Belgium also culled chickens.
These two reports make me say: may God have mercy on you, Dr. Diaa.
Today, the Al-Tayyibat system has become widely known and has a large presence across social media.
Almost everyone is asking others about it,
whether among close acquaintances or more distant circles. People ask those who started the system before them so they can learn from their experience.
It is truly an honor for me, and for many Egyptians living abroad like me,
that the person behind this different medical theory was an Egyptian from my own country.
May God have mercy on the doctor. I feel that he simplified life for us and helped us think about how our bodies work, how we deal with them, and how to choose what we believe is better before
putting anything into our stomachs. In this account, she describes the stomach as central to many
health problems people experience. She then explains her understanding of what Dr. Diaa taught, saying that insulin is
an intestinal hormone and that, in her understanding, as long as food remains in the digestive system, insulin continues to be released.
She says she believes that while insulin is active, the body has less opportunity for what she calls 'cleaning' and recovery, whereas fasting gives the body a period of rest.
She further describes her belief that during fasting the body begins dealing with damaged or unhealthy cells.
In her view, this supports recovery. She also says that simple, easy-to-digest food passes through the digestive system more easily.
She contrasts that with foods she considers unsuitable, such as leafy vegetables, milk, and white flour,
which she believes may remain longer in the digestive system, ferment, and contribute to irritation.
She says this can be associated, in her experience, with symptoms such as bloating, acidity, and reflux,
after which a person may take medication to control those symptoms.
She then says that, in her understanding, the stomach is not the only organ involved, and that the liver and brain are also affected.
She describes this as influencing many systems in the body, including skin, bones, nerves, and glands.
She presents the view that insulin plays a major role in many health problems and says that
controlling it through fasting or through what she considers simple, wholesome food may help the body return to balance.
She says that, in her understanding, the liver and brain can then function more normally and the body can begin recovering.
Her message is that fasting itself does not harm a person, whereas constantly eating large amounts without thought can, in her view, be harmful.
She then shares her personal experience: at the time of the recording, she says she had been following the system for 130 days and had gone 130 days without medication.
She says her life had changed dramatically and that she could hardly believe it, because some of the problems she had lived with had lasted for decades.
She says she had taken some medications for many years and now felt free because she was no longer taking them.
She asks God to have mercy on Dr. Diaa and says she believes he was treated unfairly and misrepresented.
She urges viewers not to accept every claim they hear from others and expresses distrust toward parts of the pharmaceutical and food industries.
She says that the mind is a blessing from God
and that people should understand, reflect, and think before believing everything they are told.
She closes by wishing everyone health and happiness. Peace be upon you and God's mercy and blessings.
